decisions.rationale: Pali10.1 begins the separate question about asassato loko (the non-eternal cosmos), distinct from sassato loko at9.1. The original source independently renders this as a new On being asked unit after completing the first eternal-cosmos question and answer. The current9.1 incorrectly includes that second question. Its ellipsis abbreviates the following repeated formula and does not erase this separately rendered item. Move the whole source unit to10.1; preserve the existing finite-cosmos list at11.1 onward.

decisions.starts: I do know. I do see.’
decisions.rationale: Pali12.2 denies that Ānanda does not know or see (na ... na jānāmi na passāmi). Pali12.3 then positively asserts knowledge and seeing (Jānāmahaṁ ... passāmī). The source prints these as distinct sentences: the negative denial followed by two affirmative sentences. Current12.3 begins with the negative denial, which belongs to12.2. Move the12.3 start to the affirmative statement; preserve the question/introduction on12.1 and the answer introduction on12.2.

decisions.rationale: The original source compresses the repeated comparison into one sentence beginning From the way this person rises to an issue and ending he is dull, not discerning, with an ellipsis before the predicate. Pali9.5 already holds both this opening and its predicate (duppañño ... nāyamāyasmā paññavā). Pali9.6–9.8 repeat the omitted explanation, and9.9 repeats the same predicate. The compressed source sentence therefore belongs on its first matching Pali row9.5. Empty9.9 into9.5, preserving the translator’s abbreviation and the complete sentence. This is supported by the predicate already present in9.5, not by punctuation alone.
